problems.source_says: The PDF says the study design and primary analyses were re-registered and links an OSF record, but does not state a registration date or establish registration before data collection. The affirmative preregistration flag is therefore not explicitly supported by the source document; this does not contradict the separately documented random assignment.
problems.quote: We re-registered our study design and primary analyses (OSF | CreativityBot: A Personalized AI Assistant to Support Creativity).
problems.locator: PDF p. 19 (page index 18), Materials and Methods, Participants, first paragraph; this is the only registration statement found in the full main text and supplement.

confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly randomly assigned human subjects to personalized, partially personalized, or generic AI assistance for developing a marketing plan.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 5, Introduction, paragraph beginning "In this study, we randomly assigned"; PDF p. 8, Fig. 1 caption.

confirmed.statement: The assignment unit is the individual and the comparison is between people receiving one of three assistant configurations; randomized within-person condition order is not applicable.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19, Participants, distinct arm counts; PDF pp. 21-22, Experimental Design, access to either assistant and assignment of participants to the partial-personalization condition.

confirmed.statement: Participants received access to GPT-4o at temperature 1 while creating their own marketing campaigns; the manipulated tool was a generative LLM used for production.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 21, Experimental Design, paragraphs beginning "Next, participants were asked" and "To complete this task"; PDF pp. 37-38 (supplement pp. 9-10), system prompts instructing the assistant to deliver the final campaign brief when requested.

confirmed.statement: The Generic AI arm uses the shared campaign-development guidance, company description, and initial campaign idea, without the added participant profile or interview summary.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 21-22, Experimental Design; PDF p. 37 (supplement p. 9), Generic AI System Prompt, compared with PDF p. 38 (supplement p. 10), Personalized AI System Prompt.

confirmed.statement: The Personalized AI arm adds the participant's cognitive, psychological, demographic, and creative profile plus a summary of their marketing experience and collaboration style.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 20-22, Demographic, Psychological, and Cognitive Measures and Experimental Design; PDF p. 38 (supplement p. 10), General Profile and Task Specific Interview Summary.

confirmed.statement: The Partially personalized AI arm uses another participant's personalization information, including the psychological profile and interview summary.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 22, Experimental Design, sentence beginning "To achieve partial personalization"; PDF p. 33 (supplement p. 5), Does Personalized AI Produce Personalized Responses?, final sentence.

confirmed.statement: The paper explicitly omits a Human Only condition; the form correctly identifies comparisons between AI configurations rather than an AI-versus-no-AI experiment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 21, Experimental Design, sentence beginning "We chose not to include a Human Only condition"; creativity-codebook.md, sections 3 and 5.

confirmed.statement: The open-chat coding is supported: participants received no guidance on interacting with the tool, exchanged messages with it, and could request a final brief.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 17, Discussion, limitations paragraph; PDF p. 19, Participants; PDF pp. 37-38 (supplement pp. 9-10), final instruction in both system prompts.

confirmed.statement: The analyzed arm counts are Generic 116, Personalized 114, and Partially personalized 101, totaling 331 after exclusions; the form correctly leaves pre-exclusion randomized counts null.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19, Participants, paragraph beginning "Of the 461 participants recruited"; PDF p. 52 (supplement p. 24), Table S2 headers, checked with PDF text and table extraction.

confirmed.statement: Random selection of campaigns for expert evaluation is a separate validation procedure and is not the basis for the main experiment's random-assignment claim.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 32 (supplement p. 4), Sensitivity Analyses, paragraph beginning "As a final validation step"; main assignment documented separately on PDF pp. 5 and 21-22.

summary: The PDF explicitly supports random assignment to three GPT-4o configurations for participants' own campaign writing. The preregistration flag lacks explicit support for timing, so the coding is refuted on that detail while criterion 1 still holds.
